things_to_force_inside_scope: Communication of discharge instructions to the patient
Transmission of the discharge letter to the patient
things_the_agent_must_not_assume: The patient always returns home after discharge
The discharge letter is always signed digitally
A follow-up appointment is always required

resolved_organization_context.organization_boundary_description: The organizational boundary includes hospital departments, healthcare professionals and internal administrative services involved in preparing and completing the patient's discharge.
resolved_organization_context.internality_rule: An activity is considered internal when it is performed by staff, systems or operational units belonging to San Marco Hospital.
resolved_organization_context.externality_rule: An activity is considered external when it is performed by the patient, family members, general practitioners, external healthcare providers, pharmacies or territorial care services.

workflow_boundary.parent_workflow_definition: Management of an inpatient hospitalization episode from admission to closure of the hospital stay.
workflow_boundary.operational_purpose: Safely conclude the patient's hospital stay by confirming clinical readiness, preparing the required documentation and communicating the care instructions needed after discharge.

primary_process_object.name: Patient discharge case
primary_process_object.why_primary: It is the main operational object whose state changes from discharge candidate to formally discharged patient.

alternative_candidates.name: Discharge letter
alternative_candidates.why_not_primary: The discharge letter is an important output of the workflow, but it does not represent the entire discharge process.

alternative_candidates.name: Hospitalization episode
alternative_candidates.why_not_primary: The hospitalization episode is broader than the discharge workflow and includes activities performed before discharge planning begins.

start_boundary.start_event_or_condition: The responsible physician determines that the patient may be clinically ready for discharge.
start_boundary.first_internal_activity: The physician starts the formal discharge assessment and verifies whether the required clinical and organizational conditions are satisfied.
what_is_before_start: General management of the hospitalization episode

end_boundary.end_event_or_condition: The patient has formally left the hospital and the discharge documentation has been completed and delivered.
end_boundary.final_internal_output_or_state: The hospitalization episode is marked as discharged in the hospital information system.
what_happens_after_end: The patient follows the prescribed therapy
The general practitioner receives or reviews the discharge information
External follow-up appointments may be performed
Territorial or home-care services may begin

included_scope.reason_included: It determines whether the discharge workflow can proceed.
It ensures that the patient's post-discharge therapy is complete and consistent.
The discharge letter is one of the principal outputs required to complete the workflow.
Pending results may affect the discharge decision or the instructions provided to the patient.
The patient must understand therapies, restrictions, warning signs and any required follow-up.

included_scope.activity_or_area: Administrative closure of the hospitalization episode
included_scope.reason_included: The discharge must be recorded in the hospital system to formally conclude the workflow.

excluded_scope.reason_excluded: These activities occur before the discharge process begins.
Follow-up visits occur after the patient has been discharged.
The hospital may activate these services, but their actual execution is performed after discharge by another organization or unit.
Billing uses information produced by the discharge process but has a different operational purpose.

upstream_workflows.name: Inpatient Clinical Care Management
upstream_workflows.relationship_to_parent: Provides the clinical history, treatments, examination results and current patient condition required to evaluate discharge readiness.
upstream_workflows.output_passed_to_parent: Updated clinical record and indication that the patient may be ready for discharge.

upstream_workflows.name: Hospital Admission Management
upstream_workflows.relationship_to_parent: Creates the hospitalization episode that will later be closed by the discharge workflow.
upstream_workflows.output_passed_to_parent: Active hospitalization record with patient, department and admission information.

downstream_workflows.name: Post-Discharge Follow-up Management
downstream_workflows.relationship_to_parent: Uses the discharge instructions to organize subsequent clinical controls.
downstream_workflows.input_received_from_parent: Discharge letter, therapy plan and recommended follow-up activities.

downstream_workflows.name: Home-Care Service Activation
downstream_workflows.relationship_to_parent: Coordinates care that must continue outside the hospital.
downstream_workflows.input_received_from_parent: Patient care needs, clinical documentation and requested territorial services.

adjacent_workflows.name: Healthcare Billing and Reimbursement
adjacent_workflows.relationship_to_parent: Receives hospitalization and discharge data to calculate costs and prepare reimbursement requests.
adjacent_workflows.reason_not_inside_parent: Its purpose is financial and administrative rather than clinical and operational discharge management.

adjacent_workflows.name: Hospital Bed Management
adjacent_workflows.relationship_to_parent: Uses the discharge status to update bed availability.
adjacent_workflows.reason_not_inside_parent: The bed-management workflow reacts to the discharge but manages hospital capacity independently.

confirmation_questions.question: Should the workflow end when the patient physically leaves the department or only after the hospitalization episode is administratively closed in the hospital system?
confirmation_questions.why_needed: The physical departure and the administrative closure may occur at different times.
confirmation_questions.impact_if_unresolved: The end boundary and final internal activity would remain ambiguous.

confirmation_questions.question: Should the activation of home-care or territorial services be included when hospital staff must complete it before the patient can leave?
confirmation_questions.why_needed: Some service activations may be mandatory discharge prerequisites rather than downstream activities.
confirmation_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Activities that are operationally necessary for discharge could be incorrectly excluded.

confirmation_questions.question: Is medication delivery by the hospital pharmacy part of this workflow or managed through a separate pharmaceutical workflow?
confirmation_questions.why_needed: The organizational responsibility for discharge medication may differ between hospitals.
confirmation_questions.impact_if_unresolved: The included scope and relationship with the pharmacy workflow may be defined incorrectly.
